It offers practical advice on incorporating local soil conditions – known to affect the strength of shaking – into earthquake simulations, to help make them more realistic.\n \nFelipe was presented the award at the National Conference on Earthquake Engineering last week in Portland, Oregan.\n \nWe're delighted to fund Felipe’s outstanding research and see it recognised on the international stage 👏\n \nRead more about Felipe on our website: https://lnkd.in/g5kqpp8u","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_huge-congrats-to-dr-felipe-kuncar-who-has-activity-7485167802346299392-ZVdn"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/naturalhazardscommission"},"datePublished":"2026-07-19T23:50:09.530Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_what-would-lead-an-experienced-civil-engineer-activity-7484756499588689920-KEOT","text":"What would lead an experienced civil engineer to leave professional practice and pursue a PhD in earthquake engineering?  \n\nFor Sirodom Somboon, it started with witnessing the aftermath of the deadly 2025 Mandalay (Myanmar) earthquake firsthand. Through an NHC Toka Tū Ake-funded project led by Professor Santiago Pujol at University of Canterbury, he is investigating practical retrofit solutions that could help make these buildings more resilient to future shaking.  \n\n“I hope my work can bridge the gap between research and practice, making seismic strengthening more accessible and economically feasible in real-world applications,” he says.\n\nSirodom is our featured researcher for July. Many homeowners don't find out until after an event.\n\nOver the past few months, we've been working behind the scenes in homes across Auckland, turning properties damaged by natural hazards into practical, easy-to-understand guidance about NHCover.\n\nThis work wouldn't have been possible without Auckland Council, who opened the door to a unique opportunity to film in properties that tell a very real story about risk, damage and recovery.\n\nToday, we're sharing the first video in our Know Your Cover series, designed to help homeowners better understand what NHCover covers - and where the limits are.\n\nA huge thank you to our talented and knowledgeable colleagues, Andrew Martin and Annah Chisholm, who brought their expertise, passion and energy to the screen. But what you can’t see might matter most. The slope behind it. The water that used to flow through it. The ground it’s sitting on. These are the things that rarely show up in a property listing but can have huge consequences later. \n\nWith the support of Auckland Council, we were able to film in real properties with real hazard histories. Places that tell a much deeper story about what to look for when buying a home. The result is a video that walks through how to spot potential risks, and how to do your research.  \n\nThe conversation is led by team members across our organisation. From flood risk to earthquake vulnerability and unstable land, we talk through what to look out for at each property and how to research the natural hazard risk in the surrounding areas, helping home buyers make informed choices for them and their whānau.  \n\nA huge shoutout to Caleb Dunne, Alex Cartwright, Alex Bygrave and Andrew Martin for sharing their expertise in the film. planning.\n\nYou’ll learn about the laws that help manage natural hazards in New Zealand, such as the Building Act, Local Government Act, Resource Management Act and its replacements – the Planning Zealanders living with natural hazards. Ursula is actively working on the project after receiving the grant earlier this year.\n \nScience communication is critical to our mahi. As research funders, we want to turn the complex science we invest in into practical insights that helps New Zealand prepare for natural hazards – from everyday decisions around the home, to big choices about where and how we build. \n \nThanks to SCANZ for partnering with us to deliver this special award, which supports excellence in natural hazards science communication in memory of our shared friend and colleague.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_we-were-proud-to-be-at-the-science-communicators-activity-7478209206295244800-M247"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/naturalhazardscommission"},"datePublished":"2026-07-01T00:59:10.134Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/naturalhazardscommission_this-week-marks-five-years-since-the-partnership-activity-7477888497110986753-vSTH","text":"This week marks five years since the partnership between NHC Toka Tū Ake (then EQC) and New Zealand's private insurers went live to make the natural hazard claims experience simpler and more joined up for homeowners.\n\nSince 2021, more than 23,000 natural hazard claims have been managed through the partnership, with more than $455 million in NHCover entitlements delivered to homeowners affected by floods, storms, landslips and earthquakes.\n\nWhile those numbers are significant, they represent something much more important – thousands of New Zealanders supported through some of the most challenging times in their lives.\n\nThis milestone reflects the commitment and collaboration of many people over the past five years. Lucy’s doctoral thesis explored Indigenous perspectives on climate adaptation and intergenerational resilience.
 
We are proud to have funded Lucy’s research through our support of Te Toi Whakaruruhau o Aotearoa, the Mātauranga Māori Disaster Risk Reduction Centre. Lucy’s examiners described her thesis as "exemplary and a pleasure to read" and an "important and timely contribution" to understanding Indigenous perspectives on climate adaptation. She graduated on the Dean’s list and her thesis received no emendations!

Many of us were also fortunate to work alongside Lucy when she joined our team for several months this year. She contributed to a range of projects, including local government submissions, the Natural Hazards Portal and hazard scenarios, and was valued for her fresh thinking, tenacity and willingness to challenge and improve ideas.
 
Ngā mihi nui, Lucy, on this outstanding achievement. We’re excited to see what you do next 😊👏</p>

We're delighted to fund Felipe’s outstanding research and see it recognised on the international stage 👏

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">What would lead an experienced civil engineer to leave professional practice and pursue a PhD in earthquake engineering?  

For <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/sirodom-somboon-133238396?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Sirodom Somboon</a>, it started with witnessing the aftermath of the deadly 2025 Mandalay (Myanmar) earthquake firsthand. As part of an investigation team assessing damaged buildings, he saw how design, materials and construction quality all contribute to whether a building makes it through. 

That experience inspired Sirodom to do research into improving the safety of older concrete buildings. Through an NHC Toka Tū Ake-funded project led by Professor <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/santiago-pujol-449619236?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Santiago Pujol</a> at <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/school/university-of-canterbury/?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>University of Canterbury</a>, he is investigating practical retrofit solutions that could help make these buildings more resilient to future shaking.  

“I hope my work can bridge the gap between research and practice, making seismic strengthening more accessible and economically feasible in real-world applications,” he says.

Sirodom is our featured researcher for July. Read his story: <a class="link" href="https://lnkd.in/e2ybjCtX?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>https://lnkd.in/e2ybjCtX</a></p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        attributed-text-segment-list__content-truncated" dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Do you know what your insurance covers for natural hazards? Many homeowners don't find out until after an event.

Over the past few months, we've been working behind the scenes in homes across Auckland, turning properties damaged by natural hazards into practical, easy-to-understand guidance about NHCover.

This work wouldn't have been possible without <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/auckland-council?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Auckland Council</a>, who opened the door to a unique opportunity to film in properties that tell a very real story about risk, damage and recovery.

Today, we're sharing the first video in our Know Your Cover series, designed to help homeowners better understand what NHCover covers - and where the limits are.

A huge thank you to our talented and knowledgeable colleagues, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/andrew-martin-7b0828223?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Andrew Martin</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/annah-chisholm-b3a0a9ab?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Annah Chisholm</a>, who brought their expertise, passion and energy to the screen. And a big shout out to our fantastic film crew - <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/bvgnz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Bryce Groves</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/paul-dodge-8ab3a633?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Paul Dodge</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/nina-wells-0a950467?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Nina Wells</a> - whose creativity, hard work and direction brought these stories to life.</p>

        attributed-text-segment-list__content-truncated" dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">You’ve found a home you love. But what you can’t see might matter most. The slope behind it. The water that used to flow through it. The ground it’s sitting on. These are the things that rarely show up in a property listing but can have huge consequences later. 

With the support of <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/auckland-council?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Auckland Council</a>, we were able to film in real properties with real hazard histories. Places that tell a much deeper story about what to look for when buying a home. The result is a video that walks through how to spot potential risks, and how to do your research.  

The conversation is led by team members across our organisation. From flood risk to earthquake vulnerability and unstable land, we talk through what to look out for at each property and how to research the natural hazard risk in the surrounding areas, helping home buyers make informed choices for them and their whānau.  

A huge shoutout to <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/calebdunne?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Caleb Dunne</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/alexcartwright1?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Alex Cartwright</a>, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/alex-bygrave-a0406971?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Alex Bygrave</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/andrew-martin-7b0828223?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Andrew Martin</a> for sharing their expertise in the film. And a massive thank you to Tanya Bidois, a passionate advocate for homeowners affected by landslides who adds her firsthand experience to the story. </p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Are you a planner or policy professional keen to build your skills in managing natural hazard risk?

We’ve partnered with <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/victoria-university-of-wellington-a036a8324?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Victoria University of Wellington</a> and <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/new-zealand-planning-institute?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>New Zealand Planning Institute</a> to launch a set of short courses designed to support better land-use planning.

These micro-credential courses focus on practical skills you can apply in your day-to-day work and can even count towards the new Master of Natural Hazards Science and Policy programme.

Developed by Dr <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/wendy-saunders-b9463228?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Wendy Saunders</a> and others from across NHC Toka Tū Ake, the courses draw on our expertise in risk reduction and land-use planning.

You’ll learn about the laws that help manage natural hazards in New Zealand, such as the Building Act, Local Government Act, Resource Management Act and its replacements – the Planning Bill and Natural Hazards Environment Bill, as well as how effective policy is developed, and how to apply it to reduce risk.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">We were proud to be at the <a class="link" href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/science-communicator-s-association-of-new-zealand-scanz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Science Communicators' Association of New Zealand SCANZ</a> conference to commemorate Fleur Templeton, a science communicator in our team and a member of SCANZ, who passed away in 2024.
 
We were there to formally present the Fleur Templeton Award to winner <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/ursula-cochran-35789784?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Ursula Cochran</a>, for her project “Living Healthily with Natural Hazards” – a mental health resource to support New Zealanders living with natural hazards. Ursula is actively working on the project after receiving the grant earlier this year.
 
Science communication is critical to our mahi. As research funders, we want to turn the complex science we invest in into practical insights that helps New Zealand prepare for natural hazards – from everyday decisions around the home, to big choices about where and how we build. 
 
Thanks to SCANZ for partnering with us to deliver this special award, which supports excellence in natural hazards science communication in memory of our shared friend and colleague.</p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">This week marks five years since the partnership between NHC Toka Tū Ake (then EQC) and New Zealand's private insurers went live to make the natural hazard claims experience simpler and more joined up for homeowners.

Since 2021, more than 23,000 natural hazard claims have been managed through the partnership, with more than $455 million in NHCover entitlements delivered to homeowners affected by floods, storms, landslips and earthquakes.

While those numbers are significant, they represent something much more important – thousands of New Zealanders supported through some of the most challenging times in their lives.

This milestone reflects the commitment and collaboration of many people over the past five years. Thank you to the <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/icnz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Insurance Council of New Zealand Te Kāhui Inihua o Aotearoa(ICNZ)</a>, our insurer partners, and everyone across NHC who has helped shape, strengthen and continuously improve the claims model that is based on homeowners at the centre. 

As we look ahead, we'll continue building on what we've learned, strengthening our readiness and working together to support New Zealanders when natural hazard events occur.
